results.evidence: The park's Royal Basin page gives the trail's elevation change as 2,550 ft to 5,100 ft (trailhead to Royal Lake). A trail database gives the trail's low point (the trailhead) as 2,534 ft, and a 2002 trip report gives the starting point as c.2,500 ft. The 2,900 ft pin elevation is the outlier.

results.fact: Line climbed from the upper basin (Honeymoon couloir vs standard gully)
results.correct_value: The Honeymoon line leaves the northeast-face snow slope below the Deception-Martin low point by a left-branching gully; it does not go via Deception Basin to the east ridge.
results.evidence: A 2002 trip report describes the normal route as climbing the snow finger to the low point of the ridge, and the Honeymoon Route as a variation that climbs nearly to the low point then takes a left-branching snow gully, traverses left and climbs a second gully to the summit ridge. A 2007 Honeymoon trip report likewise climbs from upper Royal Basin to the Martin-Deception notch area and drops into the Honeymoon gully on the Royal Basin side, and a 2002 WTA report describes the snowfield on the west edge of the NE face with a band breaking left into the gully around 6,700 ft. The 'left of two gullies from Deception Basin to the east ridge' description belongs to the separate Deception Basin route on the other side of the peak.

patches.fact: Line climbed from the upper basin (Honeymoon couloir vs standard gully)
patches.find: From the upper basin, leave the trail and ascend scree/talus into Deception Basin, then climb the left (west) of two gullies just right of a large rock buttress. Follow that gully system up to Mount Deception's east ridge about 150 yards southeast of the summit and follow the ridge to the top; the scramble from Deception Basin takes roughly 3 hours.
patches.replace: From the upper basin, leave the trail and head southwest over the moraine to the big snow slope on the west edge of the northeast face. Climb it most of the way toward the low point of the Deception-Martin ridge, then break left into the steep side gully that gives the route its name; from its top, traverse left and climb a second snow-and-rock gully to the summit ridge. Allow roughly 3 hours from the upper basin to the top of the gully in good snow.

patches.replace: From the upper basin, leave the trail and cross the moraine southwest to the snow slope on the west edge of Deception's northeast face, where the climb begins. Allow about three hours from the upper basin to the top of the gully.

patches.fact: Line climbed from the upper basin (Honeymoon couloir vs standard gully)
patches.find:
From the flat in Deception Basin, climb scree and talus to the northwest and look for a LARGE ROCK BUTTRESS. Immediately right of that buttress there are TWO gullies. Take the LEFT (west) one.

The buttress is what identifies the pair — do not try to identify the gully on its own, because there is more than one gully-shaped thing in the basin. Left of two, immediately right of a big buttress.

Follow that gully system up to Mount Deception's east ridge, arriving roughly 150 yards southeast of the summit, then follow the ridge to the top. Reaching the ridge that close to the summit is the confirmation you took the right gully; topping out much further along the ridge means you were in the wrong one.
patches.replace:
From the upper basin tarn, cross the moraine southwest to the large snow slope (mud and scree once it melts out) on the west edge of Deception's northeast face, and climb it toward the low point of the Deception-Martin ridge.

Do not go all the way to that low point: the ridge crest there is the standard route, which drops onto the small glacier beyond and circles Gilhooley Tower. Arriving on the crest at the low point means you have passed the branch.

results.evidence: Documented ascents are a May 2026 party (WTA report, good snow in the couloir) and a June 23, 2007 party, plus an Aug 26, 2002 ascent in largely melted-out conditions that the climber would not recommend. No two sources state whether spring (May) or late June is the better window, so the spring-vs-late-June and May 'risky' disagreement cannot be settled; the late-summer 'worse' part is agreed by all fields.

The park's wilderness-reservations page says summer-season reservations (May 15 - Oct 15) release April 15, with high-elevation areas limited to a shorter season (typically mid-July to mid-October); its Royal Basin page says early reservations are recommended for trips May 1 - Sept 30. Nothing supports a June 15 opening, but both statements come from one publisher, so no two independent sources settle the date. Recommend dropping 'Royal Basin permits open June 15' once confirmed.

No source states a car-to-car gain for the Honeymoon Route. Trip reports give ~18 miles round trip, trailhead c.2,500 ft and summit 7,788 ft, which makes 7,861 ft look high, but the rules forbid computing a replacement from trailhead/summit arithmetic.
